To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the grain size of a deformed material is determined by the temperature-strain-rate condition of the deformation, and that the structure formed at a given temperature and strain rate is stable only if it has been formed under conditions corresponding to the dynamic recrystallizaton mechanism.

(a) grain growth in the ultrafine structure of copper and iron depends on the temperature-strain rate conditions of plastic deformation and (b) the structure obtained by dynamic recrystallisation is unstable upon heating

the effect of temperature-strain rate conditions on the stability of ultrafine structure upon heating is determined by the mechanism of its creation (dynamic recrallization or work-hardening) and depends on the temperature-strain rate parameters of the plastic deformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the temperature-strain-rate condition of plastic deformation on the stability of the structure of copper and iron upon heating.
the effect of temperature-strain rate conditions on the formation of ultrafine structures in copper and iron and their stability upon heating.
the effect of temperature-strain rate conditions of plastic deformation on the stability of the ultrafine structure obtained by dynamic recrystallisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of a structure upon heating depends on the temperature-strain-rate parameters of the plastic deformation that led to the formation of this structure.
the stability of an ultrafine grained structure upon heating is not determined by the temperature-strain-rate parameters of its formation but by the mechanism of its origin.

the stability upon heating of an ultrafine structure formed by shear deformation under high pressure is determined by its mechanism of formation (dynamic recry-stallization or work-hardening) which in turn is determined by the temperature and strain rate conditions of plastic deformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of an ultrafine-grained structure depends on the conditions of its formation and the temperature-strain-rate regime of subsequent annealing.
the structure of the material is stable upon heating if the temperature-rate conditions are such as to produce dynamic recovery.
a thermally stable ultrafine structure can be obtained by shear deformation at high temperatures under pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high-temperature structure can be formed only if the material is deformed at a temperature above the recrystallizing one.
a structure with high-angle grain boundaries is thermally stable only when it is formed by the work hardening mechanism.
the stability of the ultrafine structure depends on its formation mechanism.
